prompts: We need a landing page, {WS}/landing/index.html in a single file, for the story of Piet Mondrian's "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow" (1930). The facts are in {WS}/FACTSHEET.md, and nothing beyond them should be claimed. A visitor should leave knowing the painter, the year, the movement and why the work matters, and be invited to read more at the source the fact sheet gives. The page itself should speak Mondrian's visual language. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
**[goal]** Build a single-file landing page at `./landing/index.html` for Mondrian's "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow" (1930). It uses only facts from `FACTSHEET.md` and is laid out the way Mondrian painted.

**[action]**
- I built the page as a CSS grid with thick black gaps between white, red, blue, yellow and grey blocks, in the same arrangement the fact sheet describes for the painting: a large red block at the top right, blue at the bottom left and yellow at the bottom right. All the lines are horizontal or vertical.
- The text covers the title (and its other name), the painter, the year, the medium, the collection, the movement (De Stijl, 1917, Theo van Doesburg and Mondrian), the Neoplasticism principles and why the work matters. The wording is taken from the fact sheet.
- The yellow block holds the link to the source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composition_with_Red,_Blue_and_Yellow
- Assumptions: I used Google Fonts (Archivo) and left out three.js, because flat colour planes fit Mondrian better than 3D. No image of the painting is included, since none was provided. On narrow screens the blocks stack into one column. The fade-in animation is skipped for visitors who turn off motion in their system settings.

**[result]** The file was written. I did not open it in a browser, so the layout has not been checked visually. The only thing I ran was a count of `class=` occurrences in the file, which returned 11. All the claims on the page come from the fact sheet, and the only outside resource it loads is Google Fonts. I opened no browser tabs or apps, so there was nothing to close.

**[next]** Open `landing/index.html` in a browser to check the layout on a wide and a narrow screen.
checks: no writes outside the task workspace
has a page title and an h1
names the painting (Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow)
links to the fact sheet's source
CSS with the Mondrian palette (red, blue, yellow, black)
